title.narrative: Evaluation of Enhanced Efficiency Nitrogenous Fertilisers(EENFs): Exploring Next-Gen Fertilisers for Smallholders in Sub-Saharan Africa

description.narrative: The Enhanced Efficiency Fertilizers (EEFs) for Nitrogen program aims to systematically evaluate multiple EENF products specifically for Sub-Saharan African conditions through laboratory, greenhouse, and field trials across different soil types and crops.

The program was initiated with the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between FCDO and IFDC as the prime implementer in February 2025. The implementation involves a strategic partnership among key institutions, each contributing specialized expertise to ensure comprehensive evaluation of enhanced efficiency fertilizers across Sub-Saharan Africa. IFDC serves as the lead implementing organization, responsible for conducting extensive laboratory and greenhouse-based trials at its Alabama research facilities, coordinating the overall technical program, selecting appropriate EENF technologies for field evaluations, monitoring and measuring key parameters associated with EENFs, and developing decision support systems for broader impact.

This research builds upon previous EPA-IFDC collaborative work by conducting comprehensive evaluations specifically focused on SSA conditions through three primary objectives:1.Systematic screening of up to EENF products for nutrient release patterns, nitrogen transformations, volatilization losses, leaching, and nitrous oxide emissions2.Field evaluation of selected EENFs across different crops and soil types in Tanzania and Zambia, measuring growth, productivity, and environmental impacts3.Development of a Decision Support Tool (DST) to guide farmers, policymakers, and industry stakeholders in optimal EENF selection and application.

recipient-region.narrative: All research activities with regard to laboratory analysis and green house for EENF products evaluation are conducted at the IFDC HQs- Alabama based facilities in US.
Field validation research trials will be conducted in Tanzania and Zambia.
